newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks hit new highs as rally continues.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks hit new highs as rally continues.

* Toronto stocks enjoyed a record session on Wednesday, extending Tuesday's gains * Fed's Greenspan repeated no immediate need for rate hike * 103 million shares traded.
Toronto stocks ventured into record territory on Wednesday amid expectations that Canadian and U.S. interest rates would not move higher soon.
The TSE 300 Composite Index added 50.91 points to finish at 6765.16, surpassing the previous record close on July 17.
The key index also reached an intraday peak of 6767.14.

"It's just a continuation of Tuesday's market. The same stocks were moving the market. The banks, Bell, Northern Telecom," said Rolie Bradley, an institutional salesman with Maison Placements Canada Inc.
About 103 million shares were traded worth C$1.8 billion.

U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sparked a rally in North American stock and bond markets on Tuesday when he told Congress that rowth in the economy had moderated and suggested that any rise in interest rates to head off inflation would not be needed in the near future.
Greenspan repeated those comments to the Senate Banking committee on Wednesday.
Toronto posted gains in all but two of 14 sub-groups, precious metals and communications. The strong side was led by conglomerates, base metals and consumer products.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Northern Telecom Ltd jumped 6.75 to 141.75 after a U.S. brokerage house raised its 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for the telecommunications giant.
* BCE Inc, Canada's largest publicly traded firm, gained 0.20 to 42.10 after reporting stronger second-quarter results.
* Canadian Pacific Ltd climbed 2.20 to close at 42.10, off a 52-week high of 42.15 earlier today, after the company reported sharply higher second-quarter railway income.
* Toronto Dominion Bank added 0.35 to 44.75. Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce hit a 52-week high of 41.75 before turning lower on the day. CIBC fell 0.95 to end at 39.70.
